A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MonarchAttention work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Appendices A–D are retained, and v2 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-conversion experiments for image classification, question answering, summarization, and image generation, together with GPU runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original convergence, layer-ablation, post-swap fine-tuning, and graph node-classification results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The variational objective, Monarch factorization, identity initialization, alternating updates (7)–(10), padding procedure, and fused kernels remain unchanged. Derivation and pseudocode corrections do not introduce a different algorithm; the new experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds Actor graph node classification using GraphGPS, extending coverage beyond images and language to graph data. The original ImageNet, SQuAD1.1, and BookSum coverage remains. The graph evaluation measures training accuracy only.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged: linear attention, Performer, cosFormer, Nyströmformer, softmax, and FlashAttention-2 retain their respective roles. The added BART and graph comparisons reuse Nyströmformer and softmax rather than introducing new comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds post-swap BART fine-tuning at 8192 tokens, individual-layer RoBERTa tests, DiT quarter-replacement tests, and a GraphGPS protocol with 1500 training steps and training-split evaluation. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; iteration counts newly emphasized in the main text were already documented in v1's appendices.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds variational-objective convergence measurements, individual-layer RoBERTa sensitivity, and a comparison of fine-tuned versus zero-shot BART performance. It also extends v1's DiT whole/half-layer comparisons with quarter-specific ablations, substantially expanding diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 0 and shared random inputs for DiT in Appendix D.5. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests, and the new appendix introduces no additional statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 and Figure 8 add convergence values, layerwise F1, quarter-specific FID/sFID, fine-tuning ROUGE, and graph accuracy results. Original main results remain unchanged. However, Table 5's purported copied 8192-token MonarchAttention/softmax reference scores, 34.60/35.57, disagree with approximately 33.94/34.76 in the retained Figure 3; the PDFs do not explain this discrepancy.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the entropy decomposition from negative to positive weighted entropy terms. Appendix C.1 repairs the c_R definition and the R-update normalization expression. These are localized mathematical corrections; the final updates, complexity claims, and derivation framework remain intact.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains zero-shot, hardware-efficient approximation of softmax attention using Monarch matrices. The abstract and introduction retain the same complexity, transferability, and headline 1.4x/4.5x/8.2x speedup claims. Added experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds substantive discussion of autoregressive decoding limitations, possible prefill and diffusion-language-model applications, and limitations of uniformly sized Monarch blocks. Appendix E adds interpretations concerning convergence, layer sensitivity, and fine-tuning stability, while explicitly explaining the graph experiment's use of training accuracy because held-out performance was poor.

D1.justification: v2 documents ViT's patch-grid rationale and CLS-token padding, specifies random Q/K/V inputs for timing, fixes missing quotation marks in Figure 7, and supplies GraphGPS model and training hyperparameters. Existing code access, checkpoint identifiers, dataset references, and principal experimental recipes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Actor/Geom-GCN, GraphGPS, and alpha-entmax: Pei et al., Rampášek et al., and Peters et al. The main positioning against efficient-attention methods and Monarch Mixer is retained. FlashAttention-2's publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix E and corresponding cross-references, reorganizes the conclusion into three topical paragraphs, and clarifies the optimization motivation and relationship between naive and fused implementations. Most existing prose and the main section order are retained.

P2.justification: Appendix E substantially expands the experimental displays with convergence, layer-ablation, and fine-tuning tables (Tables 3–6), plus the GraphGPS accuracy–FLOPs plot (Figure 8). Existing figures and tables are retained, with resizing, page reflow, and changed float placement.

improvement.justification: The corrected derivation and pseudocode, targeted convergence and layer diagnostics, and clearer applicability limits make the method easier to assess and use. The net gain is limited: the graph evidence concerns training accuracy only, and Table 5's disagreement with Figure 3 weakens confidence in the fine-tuning comparison. These qualifications temper the benefits without negating the independent corrections and diagnostic additions.
